# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

//! ## TinyTemplate
//!
//! TinyTemplate is a minimal templating library originally designed for use in [Criterion.rs].
//! It deliberately does not provide all of the features of a full-power template engine, but in
//! return it provides a simple API, clear templating syntax, decent performance and very few
//! dependencies.
//!
//! ## Features
//!
//! The most important features are as follows (see the [syntax](syntax/index.html) module for full
//! details on the template syntax):
//!
//! * Rendering values - `{ myvalue }`
//! * Conditionals - `{{ if foo }}Foo is true{{ else }}Foo is false{{ endif }}`
//! * Loops - `{{ for value in row }}{value}{{ endfor }}`
//! * Customizable value formatters `{ value | my_formatter }`
//! * Macros `{{ call my_template with foo }}`
//!
//! ## Restrictions
//!
//! TinyTemplate was designed with the assumption that the templates are available as static strings,
//! either using string literals or the `include_str!` macro. Thus, it borrows `&str` slices from the
//! template text itself and uses them during the rendering process. Although it is possible to use
//! TinyTemplate with template strings loaded at runtime, this is not recommended.
//!
//! Additionally, TinyTemplate can only render templates into Strings. If you need to render a
//! template directly to a socket or file, TinyTemplate may not be right for you.
//!
//! ## Example
//!
//! ```
//! #[macro_use]
//! extern crate serde_derive;
//! extern crate tinytemplate;
//!
//! use tinytemplate::TinyTemplate;
//! use std::error::Error;
//!
//! #[derive(Serialize)]
//! struct Context {
//!     name: String,
//! }
//!
//! static TEMPLATE : &'static str = "Hello {name}!";
//!
//! pub fn main() -> Result<(), Box<Error>> {
//!     let mut tt = TinyTemplate::new();
//!     tt.add_template("hello", TEMPLATE)?;
//!
//!     let context = Context {
//!         name: "World".to_string(),
//!     };
//!
//!     let rendered = tt.render("hello", &context)?;
//! #   assert_eq!("Hello World!", &rendered);
//!     println!("{}", rendered);
//!
//!     Ok(())
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! [Criterion.rs]: https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs
//!

/// The default format.
///
/// This format needs to work with any combination of crate features.
struct ConfigurableFormatWriter<'a> {
    format: &'a ConfigurableFormat,
    buf: &'a mut Formatter,
    written_header_value: bool,
}

impl ConfigurableFormatWriter<'_> {
    fn write(mut self, record: &Record<'_>) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.write_timestamp()?;
        self.write_level(record)?;
        self.write_module_path(record)?;
        self.write_source_location(record)?;
        self.write_target(record)?;
        self.finish_header()?;

        self.write_args(record)?;
        #[cfg(feature = "kv")]
        self.write_kv(record)?;
        write!(self.buf, "{}", self.format.suffix)
    }

    fn subtle_style(&self, text: &'static str) -> SubtleStyle {
        #[cfg(feature = "color")]
        {
            StyledValue {
                style: if self.buf.write_style == WriteStyle::Never {
                    style::Style::new()
                } else {
                    style::AnsiColor::BrightBlack.on_default()
                },
                value: text,
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "color"))]
        {
            text
        }
    }

    fn write_header_value<T>(&mut self, value: T) -> io::Result<()>
    where
        T: Display,
    {
        if !self.written_header_value {
            self.written_header_value = true;

            let open_brace = self.subtle_style("[");
            write!(self.buf, "{open_brace}{value}")
        } else {
            write!(self.buf, " {value}")
        }
    }

    fn write_level(&mut self, record: &Record<'_>) -> io::Result<()> {
        if !self.format.level {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let level = {
            let level = record.level();
            #[cfg(feature = "color")]
            {
                StyledValue {
                    style: self.buf.default_level_style(level),
                    value: level,
                }
            }
            #[cfg(not(feature = "color"))]
            {
                level
            }
        };

        self.write_header_value(format_args!("{level:<5}"))
    }

    fn write_timestamp(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
        #[cfg(feature = "humantime")]
        {
            use self::TimestampPrecision::{Micros, Millis, Nanos, Seconds};
            let ts = match self.format.timestamp {
                None => return Ok(()),
                Some(Seconds) => self.buf.timestamp_seconds(),
                Some(Millis) => self.buf.timestamp_millis(),
                Some(Micros) => self.buf.timestamp_micros(),
                Some(Nanos) => self.buf.timestamp_nanos(),
            };

            self.write_header_value(ts)
        }
        #[cfg(not(feature = "humantime"))]
        {
            // Trick the compiler to think we have used self.timestamp
            // Workaround for "field is never used: `timestamp`" compiler nag.
            let _ = self.format.timestamp;
            Ok(())
        }
</output>

crowbook reads the file, splits into chapters list (lines starting with `+`) and "other" lines. Hmm.

I recall crowbook's book file format:

```
# Crowbook book file
title: My Book
author: Me

## Chapters
+ chapter1.md
+ chapter2.md

## Options
...
```

/// An error that happened serializing or deserializing YAML data.
pub struct Error(Box<ErrorImpl>);

    SequenceInMergeElement,
    EmptyTag,
    FailedToParseNumber,

import pty,os,sys,fcntl,termios,struct
def run(cmd, cols=40, rows=20):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()

    fn term_w(cmd: &'cmd Command) -> usize {
        let term_w = match cmd.get_term_width() {
            Some(0) => usize::MAX,

            None => {
                let (current_width, _h) = dimensions();
                current_width.unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
            }
        };

        let max_term_w = match cmd.get_max_term_width() {
            Some(0) => usize::MAX,
            Some(mw) => mw,
            None => 100,
        };

        cmp::min(term_w, max_term_w)
    }

import pty,os
def run(args, cols=80):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execvp("/workspace/executable", ["/workspace/executable"]+args)
    out=b""
    while True:

print("=== fancy no emoji:", repr(run(["book.book"])[-200:]))
print("=== fancy emoji:", repr(run(["-f","book.book"])[-200:]))
EOF"}

F='QQFILEQQ'
def run(args):

    return r.stdout.decode()

    for line in s.split('\n'):
        if line.startswith('ERROR '):
            return line[6:]
    raise Exception(s)
open('/tmp/gen/c.book','w').write('title: T\n+ %s\n' % F)

    data[l+'book'] = errmsg(run(["-L",l,"c.book"]))
    data[l+'image'] = errmsg(run(["-L",l,"i.book"]))
    data[l+'cover'] = errmsg(run(["-L",l,"cv.book"]))
for l in ('en','fr'):
    msgs = [data[l+'book'], data[l+'image'], data[l+'cover']]
    idxs = [m.find(F) for m in msgs]
    pre = msgs[0][:idxs[0]]
    assert all(m[:idxs[0]]==pre for m in msgs), (pre, msgs)
    sufs = [m[idxs[0]+len(F):] for m in msgs]
    i=0
    while all(len(x)>i and x[i]==sufs[0][i] for x in sufs):
        i+=1
    print(l, repr(pre), repr(sufs[0][:i]), sufs)
PYEOF

F='QQFILEQQ'

    r = subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable"]+args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)

#!/bin/bash
# compare the original and my binary on a set of test files
ORIG=/workspace/executable
MINE=/tmp/mine
TD=$(mktemp -d)
cp -r "$1"/* $TD/ 2>/dev/null
cd $TD
rm -f *.html *.tex *.epub
# run original
mkdir -p orig mine
cp -r $TD/* orig/ 2>/dev/null; cp -r $TD/* mine/ 2>/dev/null
(cd orig && rm -f *.html *.tex *.epub && $ORIG "${@:2}" >/dev/null 2>orig_err.txt)
(cd mine && rm -f *.html *.tex *.epub && $MINE "${@:2}" >/dev/null 2>mine_err.txt)
echo "--- stderr diff"
diff orig/orig_err.txt mine/mine_err.txt
echo "--- file diffs"
for f in $(cd orig && ls *.html *.tex *.epub 2>/dev/null); do
  if [ -f "mine/$f" ]; then
    if ! diff -q "orig/$f" "mine/$f" >/dev/null; then
      echo "DIFF in $f"
      diff "orig/$f" "mine/$f" | head -30
    fi
  else
    echo "MISSING $f"
  fi
done
echo "--- end"
SH

import subprocess, tempfile, os, shutil
def gen(book, files=None):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    for fn, content in (files or {}).items():
        open(os.path.join(d, fn),'wb').write(content if isinstance(content, bytes) else content.encode())
    open(os.path.join(d,'b.book'),'w').write(book)
    subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','b.book'], cwd=d, capture_output=True)
    out = {}
    for f in os.listdir(d):
        if f.endswith(('.tex',)):
            out[f] = open(os.path.join(d,f)).read()

* `src/cli.rs` + `src/main.rs`: clap 4.6.1 based CLI matching the original

  (byte-identical), `--print-template html.css|epub.css`, `-c/--create`,

  original's `--list-options` output (keys, types, defaults, description
  with the original line wrapping).

  error messages (`Expected a string as value for key x, found Integer(1)`,
  `expected an integer as value for key 'x', found String("foo")`, â¦).
* `src/lib/yaml.rs`: small YAML parser (mappings, sequences, flow
  collections, block scalars) that reproduces the observed
  `YAML block was not valid YAML: â¦` messages.
* `src/lib/localization*.rs`: rendering strings for en/fr/es/de/ru/ca
  (toc, chapter, part, notes, title, cover) + the French translations of
  Crowbook's own messages; the babel language table.
* `src/lib/parser.rs`: Markdown parser (headings incl. setext, paragraphs,
  hard breaks, emphasis/strong/strike with a CommonMark-like delimiter
  stack, code spans, links/images/autolinks/entities/escapes, footnotes,
  lists incl. nesting, blockquotes, tables, definition lists, rules,
  fenced/indented code, typographic cleaning incl. the French narrow
  no-break-space rules).
* `src/lib/render/html.rs`: standalone HTML and EPUB XHTML rendering.
  Byte-identical with the original for the tested documents.
* `src/lib/render/tex.rs`: LaTeX rendering; byte-identical for the tested
  documents (template in `assets/tex.tex`, packages included depending on
  the document contents, lettrine, parts, chapter labels, footnotes).
* `src/lib/render/epub.rs`: EPUB 2 container (mimetype, META-INF, OEBPS,
  content.opf, toc.ncx, nav.xhtml, chapters, stylesheet, images).
* `src/lib/book.rs`, `src/lib/render/template.rs` (mini template engine),
  `src/lib/render/highlight.rs` (approximated syntect highlighting).

## Known gaps / TODO

1. **Fancy (TTY) UI is not implemented.** In a terminal the original shows
   a spinner/progress-bar live view (`- setting options`, `Parsing chapters`
   with `â/â` bar, `Rendering...`, `â Finished`, `â epub: generated â¦`)
   followed by the plain `WARNING/ERROR` dump. Only the plain non-TTY
   behaviour (and `-n`) is reproduced. Needs a small TUI writing
   `\x1b[1A\r\x1b[2K` sequences.
2. **Syntax highlighting** only approximates syntect + InspiredGitHub:
   * operator/keyword spans do not swallow the following space
     (`= ` vs `=` â visible with `let x = 1;` in Rust);
   * the exact sublime-syntax rules for every language are not
     reproduced (unknown languages correctly fall back to plain text).
3. **EPUB** is close but not byte identical: missing the `toc.xhtml` file
   and its `navPoint`/manifest/spine entries when `rendering.inline_toc`
   is set, the nested `navPoint`s inside parts are only approximated,
   and the zip entries are *stored* (the original deflates them), so the
   archive bytes differ (the extracted contents match apart from the
   items listed above).
4. **`html.dir` (multi-file HTML)** is a stub (it always reports the
   template error the original produces when `output.html.dir` is unset,
   but does not write the files when it is set).
5. **PDF/ODT** are not implemented: `pdf` reports
   `Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex'`
   and `odt` reports `unknown format odt` like the original, but no real
   `xelatex` invocation is done.
6. Nested YAML keys in a `.book` file reproduce the observed
   `unrecognized key`/line-number pairs, but the rule was reverse
   engineered from few samples.
7. `--autograph` prompts on stdout but the French/localized prompt and the
   LaTeX/EPUB autograph rendering were not verified.
8. `crowbook.temp_dir`, `resources.base_path.*` variants other than the
   defaults are not honoured everywhere yet.

## Verification

`compile.sh` builds with `cargo build --release --offline` and installs the
binary as `./executable`. The HTML/TeX output was diffed against the
provided binary for a corpus of Markdown documents (plain text, emphasis,
lists, quotes, tables, definition lists, code blocks, footnotes, images,
links, parts, French/Spanish/German/Russian localization, initials,
inline TOC, single-file mode). Differences found are listed above.
EOF
